results.one_line: The duty is real and tightening: BSP Circular 1222 (Oct 2025) adds a reporting-governance framework with daily fines once a one-year observation period ends around late 2026. But there were only 743 money service business head offices of all types in 2022, small-firm fines are PHP 150 a day, and AMLC filing is free, so a standalone tool for small money changers is too small to sustain a business.
results.buyers: 743 MSB head offices of all types, plus 6,841 branches (7,584 offices in total) in 2022 per BSP data reported by Philstar (philstar.com/business/2023/07/05/2278647). 7,357 offices at end-2023 (Fintech News PH). Small type F money changers are probably a few hundred entities; the split by type is unverified.
results.price: A plausible price is PHP 1,500-3,000 a month for an SaaS tool, or PHP 5,000-10,000 a month for a compliance retainer (both unverified). Today type F changers pay the BSP a PHP 20,000 annual service fee (Circ. 1206), an external auditor, and an AML seminar fee (about PHP 1,000 at InCorp). Late or faulty reports cost PHP 150 a day (Circ. 1222). Total market at full uptake is about PHP 15M a year.
results.top_competitor: No Philippine product for small money changers was found. The closest are the free state channels (AMLC GoTRACS, and BSP report submission by email) and foreign bureau-de-change POS products (CurrencyXchanger, FXPlus), which have no BSP output.
results.killer: Market too small. There were 743 MSB head offices of all types in 2022 and only a few hundred small money changers. Fines are low (PHP 150 a day) and filing is free, so willingness to pay is weak.

results.one_line: State lift acts do require owners to license or register lifts, renew them and file AMC papers, with real enforcement in UP. But renewals are moving to 3-5 years with auto-generated online licences (TN 2025 amendment), penalties are small, and AMC firms, consultants, society ERPs and free state portals already absorb the job, so a standalone tracker has no paying buyer.
results.buyers: No official national count. One market site estimates over 600,000 installed lifts in India (unverified, indexbox). UP has about 16,000 lifts across about 12,600 registrations since Oct 2024, over 80% in Noida (therealtytoday). Ghaziabad has about 4,000 operating lifts, 2,991 registered at Dec 2025 (ETV Bharat). Most owners are housing societies, AOAs and commercial buildings with 1-20 lifts. AMC firms hold the portfolios.
results.price:
A reminder tool is plausibly worth only Rs 0-2,000 per society per year. Owners pay today:
- Government renewal fees: Rs 500 (Assam), Rs 1,000 per 3 years (Haryana), Rs 2,500-7,000 (Karnataka) per lift.
- Consultants: from Rs 14,999 per licence job (IncorpX).
- AMC contracts: about Rs 10,000-50,000 per lift per year, which usually bundle the paperwork.
- Lift-service CRM: Rs 20,000 a year (IndiaMART).
- Society ERPs: about Rs 5-15 per flat per month (unverified).
results.top_competitor: Free state portals (TN auto-generated online licence, UP e-portal, Haryana and Maharashtra CEI online services) combined with the lift AMC firms and OEMs that file on owners' behalf. ElevatorPlus and ADDA's AMC and Compliance Tracker overlap partly.
results.killer: The duty comes too rarely and is too cheap to miss, and existing players already absorb it. TN's 2025 amendment replaced yearly renewal with a 5-year auto-generated online licence and decriminalised penalties (max Rs 10,000). UP renews every 5 years and Haryana every 3. Karnataka's late fee is capped at Rs 2,500. AMC firms and free state portals already do the work, so no one will pay for a date-reminder tool.

results.one_line: Kenyan estate agents and advocates must register on goAML, run CDD with sanctions and PEP screening, keep a firm risk assessment, policy and MLRO register, and keep records for 7 years, and nobody sells a Kenya-specific small-firm CDD and inspection-file tool. But registration is low, FRC inspections are few, and the LSK is building its own filing module, so this is a small add-on business, not a standalone SaaS.
results.buyers: The core paying pool is a few hundred firms. The FRC's 2025 risk profiling covered 193 real estate agencies (153 medium/high risk) and 86 law firms (74 medium/high), per Business Daily, 29 Jul 2026. The FRC targeted 1,504 estate agents, but only 112 had registered by Oct 2025 (Business Daily, 21 Oct 2025). The long tail is about 17,000 practising advocates (The Star, Nov 2025); per the LSK FAQ (Aug 2026), most firms are in scope, sole practitioners included. I found no count of law firms.
results.price: Plausible price is KSh 2,500-7,500 a month per small firm (USD 20-60), or a KSh 30-60k yearly inspection-ready bundle, plus per-check ID and screening fees. Today firms use the free LSK templates and the free goAML portal. Consultants (e.g. FNJ & Associates) do risk assessments and policies at unpublished fees, probably KSh 50-300k one-off (unverified). A Nairobi AML training seat costs GBP 2,100. Kenyan property-management SaaS runs from free to about USD 77 a month.
results.top_competitor: Free regulator tools plus consultants. The LSK Compliance Hub gives template policy and guidance, the LSK ERP AML module for STR/SAR/CTR filing is in development, the FRC goAML portal handles filing, and consultancies such as FNJ & Associates do the rest. Generic KYC rails (Smile ID with IPRS/eCitizen/BRS checks, Youverify) could move down-market.
results.killer: No single killer. The biggest risk is weak demand from weak enforcement: in FY2024/25 the FRC made 44 DNFBP inspections against a target of 487, its budget was cut to KSh 570m, and only about 7% of targeted agents had registered. That is combined with the LSK building its own filing module for advocates.

results.one_line: The yearly FICA duties are real and new for item 20 dealers selling single items of R100k or more: an annual RMCP upload by 31 Oct (Directive 12), a location report (Directive 10) and draft PCC 126 for precious metals and stones. But the jeweller niche is small and generic FICA tools and templates already cover much of it.
results.buyers: No official count. Rough estimate (unverified): 300 to 1,000 jewellery, bullion and precious-metal firms meet the per-item test, and several thousand item 20 dealers in total once motor dealers and others are included. The Jewellery Association represents about 1,000 retailers and 140 wholesalers (LBMA). The FIC had about 51,020 registered institutions in total (secondary source, unverified). There is no SADPMR permit count.
results.price: About R3,000 to R6,000 a year for an annual compliance pack. Today buyers pay: Moonstone FICA Toolkit R4,995 once-off; ClearComply from R99/month (deadline tracking only); law-firm RMCPs (prices not published); nCino KYC (price on request). Fines start at R10k, and about 90% of motor-dealer fines are R100k or more.
results.top_competitor: nCino KYC (formerly DocFox): FICA KYC and screening software that already markets to high-value goods dealers. The free FIC goAML portal is only a filing channel.
results.killer: None found. The biggest risk is a small market: the per-item R100k test excludes most small jewellers and no official count exists. nCino KYC or Moonstone could add a jeweller RMCP template cheaply.

results.one_line: Small South African estate agencies face real recurring duties with real penalties: a yearly PPRA trust audit, FIC registration, the RCR, and a new yearly RMCP upload to goAML due 31 Oct under Directive 12. No tool runs the whole workflow, but the buyer pool is only a few thousand cost-sensitive firms and the auditor files the audit itself.
results.buyers: About 9,000 estate agents are registered with the FIC; 70% had filed the RCR by Apr 2025 (STBB, 23 Apr 2025, stbb.co.za/?p=40089). About 50,000 individual practitioners renewed FFCs in 2025 (Property Professional). About 65% of agencies are small businesses or sole proprietors (REBOSA/Sakeliga via BusinessTech, unverified). Estimate: 5,000-6,000 small agencies, fewer for the audit part after trust-account exemptions. No official PPRA firm count was found.
results.price: R200-450/month or R2,500-4,500/year per small agency (an estimate, not tested). Buyers pay today: Moonstone FICA Toolkit R4,995 excl VAT once, plus a minimum of 5 paid hours; IEASA compliance webinars R300/R400; the REBOSA template is free. Consultant and audit fees not found. Penalties: R20/day then a further R25,000 for a late audit; FIC fine of R266,000 on Capital Point Properties.
results.top_competitor: Moonstone FICA Toolkit (R4,995 RMCP and risk-register template kit), plus the free REBOSA RMCP template; nCino KYC Africa/TVA (client KYC) and PropWorx/PayProp (trust ledger and exemption route) cover adjacent parts
results.killer: No single killer. The biggest risk is a small, thrifty market (about 9,000 FIC-registered agents in total) that can settle for free templates or franchise head-office packs. The trust audit is filed by IRBA auditors, and the PayProp exemption route removes the audit duty for many firms.

results.one_line: About 84.6k Indonesian refill-water depots face real SLHS, lab-test and record-keeping duties, and almost none comply. No software does this job, but the buyers are price-sensitive micro-businesses, tests are cheap and enforcement is local and sporadic, so only a city-level done-for-you service with lab revenue share looks viable.
results.buyers: 84,558 registered depots as of 25 Dec 2025, of which only 4.01% (about 3,390) hold SLHS (Kemendag/Asdamindo via JawaPos, 29 Jul 2026). Kemenkes counted 77,436 depots, 2.35% with SLHS. An adjacent segment is 25,925 SPPG free-meal kitchens, 52% with SLHS in Apr 2026 (Antara/BGN).
results.price: Today owners pay about Rp40k for a Labkesda microbiology test and Rp580k for a chemistry package (Bukittinggi). The SLHS itself is free in some districts (Wonosobo). izin.co.id does not publish its SLHS service price. Plausible offers (unverified): an app at Rp25-50k/month, or a done-for-you SLHS package at Rp0.75-2M one-off plus about Rp100-150k/month for a test-and-log plan with lab revenue share.
results.top_competitor: izin.co.id paid SLHS processing service (one-off, no recurring tracking), plus the free state route through Dinkes/Puskesmas sanitarians, Labkesda labs and OSS. No software competitor found.
results.killer: Not a hard killer, but low willingness to pay. Family micro-depots skip even cheap or free compliance (96% have no SLHS). The penalty is occasional closure, mostly in Jakarta sweeps, not fines. The core work (sampling, lab test, inspection) is physical, so a pure software tool adds little value.

results.one_line: Gas checks in Romania are mandatory: ANRE Order 179/2015 requires every gas installation to be verified every 2 years, and Order 96/2023 sharpened the rules. Only EDIB-authorised firms may do this work, and each must keep an electronic job register in the format set by Annex 6. No dedicated tool exists for these firms, but distributors already run free filing platforms and suppliers send free due-date notices, which leaves only a low-value form-and-register tool for small trade firms.
results.buyers: Number of EDIB firms is not counted. The ANRE public register at portal.anre.ro/PublicLists/AtestatGN would give it, but the fetch returned an empty table. A secondary source cites about 5,700 ANRE-authorised gas firms of all types (unverified). My estimate is 1,500-4,000 EDIB holders (unverified), likely to shrink under the stricter Order 17/2026. Demand base: about 4.25 million consumption points (4,018,505 household plus 234,476 non-household, profit.ro), or roughly 2.1 million verification sheets a year.
results.price: Firms charge customers 150-250 lei per flat verification and up to 600 lei per revision (bzi.ro, brig.ro, playtech.ro). Today firms pay nothing for tools: they use paper sheets, Excel and the free distributor platforms. A plausible price is 50-150 lei (about €10-30) per firm per month (unverified).
results.top_competitor: Free distributor filing platforms, which Order 96/2023 art. 9^1 requires distributors to provide. Example: the Distrigaz Sud Rețele portal, through which 71% of sheets were reportedly filed (unverified). The distributors' due-date database and the suppliers' free 60-day notices also cover the reminder job.
results.killer: No single named killer. The biggest risk is that distributors extend their legally mandated free platforms into full digital sheet filling. Together with low value per firm (a commodity service at 150-250 lei) and an unknown, shrinking count of EDIB firms, that keeps this weak.

results.one_line: Taiwan's every-trip soil e-manifest and GPS duty is real, but the state already runs the filing for free and approved GPS vendors already own the truck relationship, so all that is left to sell is generic dispatch and billing to a small, informal trade.
results.buyers: About 15,000 gravel and soil trucks (Sinotrade, Jan 2026). The NLMA says about 6,000 are needed per day, and 4,260 were GPS-cleared by 13 Jan 2026 (NOWnews, 14 Jan 2026). There are about 140 soil yards (CTEE). No official count of hauling firms was found; the trade is fragmented and relationship-driven (NCU 2025 study).
results.price: A plausible price is NT$300-800 per truck per month (unverified). Buyers pay nothing for the state soilmove system and e-manifest app. One approved GPS vendor (瞰車大) lists its soil GPS at $380 and fleet service at $350, with no stated billing period. The money in this trade is in soil fees (about NT$184-240/m3 at yards or Taipei Port, plus about NT$237/m3 transport, before costs rose 5-10x in 2026), not admin time.
results.top_competitor: The free NLMA soilmove system and e-manifest app (plus city apps in Taoyuan and Taichung), together with NLMA-approved GPS vendors' fleet platforms such as 瞰車大 (claims 30,000+ vehicles)
results.killer: The state does the filing for free: certificate serials are issued in soilmove, and type-approved GPS boxes send data straight to the NLMA's assigned IP and port. No public API was found, and GPS vendors already in every truck can bundle dispatch. That leaves nothing compliance-specific to sell, only generic fleet software for a fragmented, informal trade.

results.one_line: UAF Circular 62 (in force since 1 June 2025) gives about 4,000 registered brokers, real-estate firms and notaries real AML duties. But fines are small, inspections are rare, Regcheq and Gesintel already sell AML SaaS, and the market tops out at a niche of roughly USD 200k a year unless broker licensing passes.
results.buyers: The UAF register at 30/06/2025 (republished by CIPER) has 8,970 entities in all: 1,383 property brokers, 2,009 real-estate management firms (many of them one-project SPVs), 496 notaries and 93 conservadores, so about 3,980 core targets. Industry estimates put active brokers at 5,000 to 20,000+ (Emol, Aug 2025), so most brokers are not registered.
results.price: No public prices were found for consultants or SaaS; Regcheq and Gesintel quote on request. My estimate (unverified) is 0.5 to 1 UF a month (CLP 20-40k) for small brokers, 1.5 to 3 UF a month for developer groups or notaries, or 3 to 6 UF for a one-off manual-and-training pack. Today's fines: 27 to 42 UF average per sanction in 2018, and 15 to 50 UF in court cases in 2025-26. The legal maximum is 800/3,000/5,000 UF, tripled for repeat breaches.
results.top_competitor: Regcheq (Chilean RegTech covering Ley 19.913 KYC, list monitoring and ROS; described as low cost; 500+ LATAM clients; no public price). Gesintel AMLupdate is the competitor for notaries. Law firms (Prieto, Carey, AZ) sell manuals and training. The free UAF portal only takes filings.
results.killer: No hard killer. The main risk is weak buying pressure: a small market (about 4,000 entities, fewer real decision-makers), small typical fines, about 1% yearly inspection odds for real-estate firms, a compliance officer who must be internal (so no outsourced-officer service), and Regcheq or Gesintel could easily move down-market.
